chapterName: Early Rome & the Kingdom: The Foundation of an Empire (753-509 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the reviewed chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What did the Latin word rex mean?
questions.explanation: Rex meant king; the Romans had seven of them before the Republic.
questions.sourceQuote: Long before any king (*rex*), the site of Rome (*Roma*) had real advantages.

questions.question: In the legend, a lupa fed the twins Romulus and Remus. What was a lupa?
questions.explanation: A she-wolf (lupa) suckled the twins in a cave called the Lupercal.
questions.sourceQuote: Instead a she-wolf (*lupa*) suckled them in a cave called the Lupercal

questions.question: Ancus Marcius founded Ostia. What does its Latin root ostium mean?
questions.explanation: Ostia lay at the mouth of the Tiber, and ostium means river mouth.
questions.sourceQuote: He founded Ostia (from *ostium*, "river mouth"), a port at the river's mouth

questions.question: The Senate (senatus) took its name from which Latin word?
questions.explanation: The Senate was a council of elders: senatus comes from senex, "old man".
questions.sourceQuote: together they formed the Senate (*senatus*, from *senex*, "old man")

questions.question: The word "republic" comes from the Latin res publica. What did it mean?
questions.explanation: Res publica meant "the public thing": the state belonged to the people, not to a king.
questions.sourceQuote: This marked the birth of the Republic (*res publica*, "the public thing").

questions.question: Rome's last king was called Superbus. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus was "Tarquin the Proud"; the earlier Tarquin was Priscus, "the Elder".

questions.question: Romans counted years ab urbe condita. What did that mean?
options: From the founding of the city
Under the rule of the kings
In the year of the consuls
Since the war with the Sabines
questions.explanation: Years were counted from Rome's traditional founding in 753 BC, abbreviated AUC.
questions.sourceQuote: the year from which Romans counted *ab urbe condita* ("from the founding of the city", abbreviated AUC)

questions.question: Tarquin the Proud was said to ignore the mos maiorum. What was it?
options: The laws of the Twelve Tables
questions.explanation: The mos maiorum, "the ways of the ancestors", was the unwritten custom Romans expected their rulers to respect.
questions.sourceQuote: ignored custom (*mos maiorum*, "the ways of the ancestors") and the Senate
